title.narrative: 48 hr Emergency Shelter and NFI Response for Displaced Populations Across High-Risk Areas of the West Bank

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtSince Oct. 2023, escalating violence and ongoing military operations in the northern West Bank—particularly in Jenin and Tulkarem camps—have caused widespread destruction, mass displacement, and severe deterioration of living conditions. According to UNRWA, approximately 33,000 Palestinians have been displaced from Jenin, Tulkarem, and surrounding communities since early 2025. Many of these families were already living in poverty and relying on social assistance prior to displacement. Ongoing displacement and economic decline have further undermined their ability to meet basic needs.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtMA’AN, through its participation in the Joint Assessment on Displacement in the Northern West Bank (May–June 2025) and rapid field-level consultations, identified winter clothing as a critical unmet need across displaced households. Female-headed households, families with children, persons with disabilities, and families who lost their primary income sources remain among the most vulnerable. In coordination with Shelter Cluster, Humanitarian Fund, UNRWA, OCHA North Office, affected communities, and Camp Service Committees, winterization support was identified as an urgent priority with limited ongoing coverage.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis project aims to provide dignified, timely, and needs-based winter support to 880 displaced families (4,136 individuals) residing in Jenin, including families hosted in the American University dormitories and those displaced within eastern Jenin neighborhoods and Al Almaniyeh. lt/pgtltpgtAssistance will be delivered through a 300 NIS e-voucher per household, redeemable through approved PalPay vendors for winter clothing. This modality ensures flexibility, supports local markets, and enables households to select items based on their specific needs. MA’AN will sign agreements with vendors to ensure that e-vouchers can only be used to purchase winter clothing, covering a variety of essential items as coordinated with the Shelter Cluster.lt/pgtltpgtThe e-voucher value is based on the clothing component of the 2025 West Bank Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), estimated at 51.9 NIS per month per household, representing the minimum clothing needs for an average family of five. Considering approximately five upcoming cold months, the total seasonal cost amounts to 260 NIS, rounded up to 300 NIS per household to accommodate price fluctuations and seasonal variations. While the voucher amount is not intended to fully cover all winter clothing needs, it is designed to contribute to the most urgent requirements, allowing families to prioritize and purchase essential items with dignity.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTo ensure complementarity and prevent duplication, MA’AN will coordinate closely with UNRWA, Shelter Cluster, OCHA North Office, and CRS. CRS is planning a similar intervention targeting internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Tulkarem. Through joint planning under the Shelter Cluster, it was agreed that MA’AN will focus on displaced families in Jenin, while CRS will target displaced families in Tulkarem. This coordination ensures geographic coverage is harmonized, avoids overlap, and maximizes the impact of the winterization response.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtMA’AN will verify at least 20% of the caseload prior to transfers and conduct continuous monitoring to ensure safe and dignified access to vendors, with oversight of transaction processes in coordination with PalPay. The project integrates protection mainstreaming, gender-sensitive approaches, and full accountability through MA’AN’s established Complaints and Response Mechanism (CRM), accessible through multiple channels and displayed at vendor locations.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtPost-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) will assess utilization, satisfaction, and market conditions, with findings shared with the Humanitarian Fund and relevant clusters. Through this intervention, MA’AN aims to enhance the well-being and protection of displaced families during the winter season by enabling access to essential winter clothing and strengthening their coping capacity amid ongoing instability.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
